title: DR1 refuses to move on until the user has entered a number of animals for every species on the consignment; the frontend accepts the field left blank and saves the blank.

finding.frontend: Number of animals is validated for shape but not for presence. The rule is integerInRange with a minimum of 1 (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/fields.js:21-24), and that validator allows the empty string through before the digit check ever runs (src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:123-131). So 'ten' is rejected and '' is accepted: Save and continue succeeds, the line is stored with an empty count, and the user reaches the rest of the journey with a consignment that says nothing about how many animals are in it. The blank is not merely tolerated, it is asserted: the feature's own test posts an empty count, expects no error re-render, and expects '' to be what the line ends up holding, treating an unanswered count as uncapped rather than zero (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.controller.test.js:150-168). What the blank does not survive is the task list — the frontend's obligation model already marks numberOfAnimalsQuantity mandatory (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js:61-66) and a blank counts as unfulfilled, so the commodities task stays incomplete. The gap is therefore inside the frontend as much as against DR1: the page lets a user past a field the service's own model says they must answer, and tells them nothing until the hub.
finding.prototype: DR1 treats the count as mandatory for every live-animal species on the page. A blank raises 'Enter the number of animals' against that species' input, and a non-numeric or non-positive value raises 'Enter a whole number greater than 0' (app/routes.js:816-848). The page re-renders with the error and nothing is saved, so a DR1 consignment cannot carry a species with no count.
finding.difference: Make Number of animals mandatory on Commodity details — one required rule per species line, with an error naming that line. The knock-on is the frontend's own count-drop check, which today reads a blank count as 'no cap' when deciding whether identifier records would be orphaned; once blank cannot be saved, that branch has no live case and the check compares two real numbers. Update the test that currently asserts the blank saves.
finding.falsifiedBy: Submitting Consignment details with Number of animals empty and being shown an error rather than being moved on.
finding.correction: The finding is correct and the test citation is exact, but the word 'deliberate' was overstated and has been replaced. Traced it three ways. The validator: integerInRange builds a Joi string with .allow(''), and an allow value short-circuits the custom digit check, so '' passes and 'ten' does not — src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:123-131 is the right range and the right reading. The controller: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.controller.js:78-108 runs the same validation for Save and continue and for Save and return to hub and then writes values[animalsField(index)] straight onto the line, so the blank really is persisted and there is no lenient-save branch. The test: consignment-details.controller.test.js:150-168 is 'Should leave a blank count out of the drop check — unanswered means uncapped, not zero'; it posts numberOfAnimalsQuantity-0 as '', asserts result.view is undefined (no error re-render) and asserts the stored value is ''. So the citation proves the behaviour, but its subject is the identifier drop check rather than the obligation, and the frontend's own obligation model marks the field mandatory — so this reads as an inconsistency between the page and the model, not as an intended design. Nothing changes in the work: a required rule per species line on the page is still the fix, and the test still has to be updated.
